title: Thousands march in Barcelona for public education and housing

tea.why: Teachers, families, and housing advocates marched to protest conditions in the public education sector and housing costs.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded a 6% GDP budget for public education, salary increases, smaller class ratios, inclusion resources, and housing rights.
tea.changed: Nov 21, 2026: Thousands marched through central Barcelona ahead of a planned teachers' strike.

summary: Thousands of people marched through the center of Barcelona to demand improvements in public education and housing rights. Convened by educational unions, associations, and the Sindicat de Llogateres, the protest started at Plaça Urquinaona and proceeded towards Plaça Sant Jaume, the seat of the Generalitat and Barcelona City Council. Participants displayed banners calling for inclusive, quality education in Catalan, higher wages, lower student-to-teacher ratios, and increased funding, while criticising the regional education department's lack of progress in negotiations. Authorities responded by stating that the academic year began with additional staff and increased resources for inclusive education, though unions maintained calls for an upcoming strike.
demands: Allocate 6% of GDP to public education
Improve teacher salaries and working conditions
Increase resources and personnel for inclusive education
Defend the Catalan linguistic immersion policy and secure housing rights
response: Authorities stated that the academic year began with over a thousand additional professionals in public schools and more than a 36% increase in personnel dedicated to inclusive education, according to reports.

crowd.text: 3,000 people according to the Urban Guard and 5,000 according to organisers

updates.text: Thousands of demonstrators marched from Plaça Urquinaona to Plaça Sant Jaume in central Barcelona.
